maya: CI red on nightly-h100-warmup job, seeing OOM in the very first warmup step across 2 shards. stack trace below, cc @devon @ryan :eyes:

maya: ```
E CUDA out of memory: 0 bytes
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "serve.py", line 42, in <module>
    allocate_kv_cache()
RuntimeError: cuda runtime error (2) : out of memory at ...
```

ci-bot: build 987654 failed on runner h100-nightly (shard 3). job logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/987654 :warning:

devon: which commit/sha is this running?

maya: running on commit abc1234 (PR #4127 merged yesterday). image: redwood/runtime:nightly-2026-03-16-gpu-540

ryan: fwiw we rolled drivers from 535 -> 540 last night in canary. could be driver/kernel mismatch causing weird allocation behavior. did the infra job pick up a mixed host driver?

sre-oncall: driver rollout started at 2026-03-16T03:10Z, target hosts on the h100 pool were updated gradually. i'll check if shard 3 landed on a host with older kernel.

anika: to triage quickly, can you try reproducing locally with reduced workload? e.g.:
```bash
# quick repro, single gpu
docker run --gpus all -e REDWOOD_ENV=ci \
  -v $(pwd):/work redwood/runtime:nightly-2026-03-16-gpu-540 \
  python -u tests/repro/warmup_repro.py --batch 1 --seq 1024
```
that should hit the same allocate_kv_cache path. also try image tag with driver 535 if you can.

maya: starting a local run now. also kicked off a CI rerun on shard 3 to see if it was a transient placement: `ci rerun 987654 --shard 3`

ci-bot: rerun scheduled for build 987654 (shard 3). queued on h100-pool-5. ETA ~3m. :play_or_pause_button:

ryan: if rerun fails, let's request a bisect across the driver bump and kernel patches between 535 and 540. maya, capture the host kernel version from the failing job logs (uname -r) and attach.

maya: got local repro on my workstation but only when I use image with gpu-540 tag. gpu-535 image passed. host kernel from failing CI: 6.2.18-rt. attaching snippet from job log: ```uname -r: 6.2.18-rt```

devon: that pattern (new driver + rt kernel) rings a bell. can you rerun with `--env CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` to get a tighter stack? also drop batch to 1 and long seq to maximize memory pressure.

maya: rerun with blocking enabled now. will paste stack if it reoccurs. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: I isolated the shard placement — it was on host h100-17 which is on driver 540 but kernel 6.2.18-rt. opening infra ticket to check module versions and nv-hostengine logs.

ci-bot: rerun finished: build 987654 (shard 3) -> FAILED again, same OOM in warmup. logs updated. :x:

anika: since rerun reproduced consistently, please open a bisect request with list: [commit range, driver versions, kernel versions, image tags]. if you want I can help run a binary search by flipping driver version on a spare host.

maya: will open bisect ticket now and add the repro steps + logs. if anyone has a spare h100 host with driver 535 we can run a quick smoke to confirm. thanks, will follow up with results. :sparkles:
